later_window.interpretation: 720p can be smooth on the healthier receiver path; sparse reports and layer/content changes prevent a controlled before/after performance claim

server.caveat: Host-namespace UDP counters do not establish container-namespace or end-to-end packet delivery

findings: Confirmed profile defect: startScreenShare captures 2560x1440/60 and applies only bitrate/framerate; resolution scaling exists only in updateScreenShareProfile. Actual receiver frames confirm the mismatch under 1080p60.
1440p contains 1.7778 times the pixels of 1080p. Extra encoding/decoding and bandwidth pressure is expected, but its individual FPS cost was not isolated.

Viewer A path impairment is independently supported by losses, RTT spikes and SFU LOSS congestion decisions. Wi-Fi, ISP routing, congestion and client stalls cannot be separated by these counters alone.
Sender FPS also varies; active simulcast layers and capture motion are not independently measured, so all sender dips cannot be attributed to network or CPU.
Presented FPS has impossible-for-target bursts above 140 while decoded FPS remains lower. Diagnose with decoded FPS; the playback counter needs visibility/window handling review.
Existing traces already contain the requested profile, platform, resolution, FPS, bitrate, loss and RTT. No additional tracing was required to establish these findings.
next_actions: Apply the selected encoder resolution on initial screen publication and verify initial 720p/1080p/1440p against actual encoded dimensions.
Repeat a bounded simultaneous moving-scene comparison after correct scaling; evaluate the impaired receiver path independently.
For remaining sender/decoder attribution, add capture FPS, active-layer identity, encode/decode time and jitter-buffer delay; keep unknown fields absent.
Forward already accepted dropped_frames/packets_lost into media.sample and review presented-FPS sampling across visibility changes.
limitations: Client reports are sparse and visibility-dependent; absent rows are not proof of disconnection or zero FPS.
Sender bitrate totals layers while each receiver reports its selected stream.
No visual stream inspection, hardware profiling, codec/QP or controlled network test was performed.
No claim that the cause of every low-FPS event or a specific local network device has been proven.
privacy: Only anonymous aggregates saved; no account/session identifiers, names, credentials, SDP, ICE addresses or media payloads.
